Subject: Initial redlines — MSA + Order Form (staffing/maintenance)

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — technical fit looks good and the team is excited. Our legal and SRE leads reviewed the MSA + Order Form and flagged a few items we need to resolve before we can route to procurement for signature:

- Maintenance windows: request to cap rolling maintenance to 4 hours/week with blackout periods for our pacific-region business hours (08:00–18:00 PT).
- Service credits: we prefer a flat 10% credit for incidents >=2 hrs, and 30% for incidents >=8 hrs; current draft has tiered, more complex math that our finance team dislikes.
- Response times: we need P1 initial response time <=30 minutes for critical incidents — please confirm on-call ladder/SLAs.

I attached our annotated redlines (pdf) — please circulate to your legal and ops. We want to keep momentum; can you confirm Redwood's flexibility on the maintenance and credit caps?

Best,
Alex Rivera
Director, Cloud Ops — EdgeCloud
attachments: OrderForm_EdgeCloud-v2.pdf (markup)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-05-09T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — MSA + Order Form (staffing/maintenance)

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the quick review on your side. High-level reply: we can get most of this into scope but need to balance availability commitments across our multi-tenant backend and reserved pools. Proposed compromise below, and looping in Kimberly (legal) + Marissa (CS/ops) to validate operational details.

Proposed Redwood positions:
- Maintenance windows: agree to blackout windows for 08:00–18:00 PT (pacific) for production endpoints tied to this order form, provided we retain the right to schedule up to 6 hours/month of rolling maintenance outside those blackout times for platform upgrades (we can offer notifications + 72-hr pre-schedule).
- Service credits: we can simplify to a two-tier credit: 15% for outages >=3 hours, 35% for outages >=9 hours (applies to monthly invoice cap of 100% of monthly fee). We prefer hour thresholds aligned with how we measure and detect incidents; we detail this in SLA-change-log.txt.
- Response times: we confirm an internal on-call ladder that targets P1 initial response <=30 minutes during business hours and <=45 minutes outside business hours for customers on this plan — will add escalation path.

Next steps: Kimberly — can you review the legal phrasing for the blackout carveout and credit cap language? Marissa — can you validate the on-call ladder + notification cadence? Alex — if you can indicate which items are going to block procurement (credits vs blackout), we can prioritize.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-05-10T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — MSA + Order Form (staffing/maintenance)

Vanessa / Alex — quick legal review after reading the proposals:

- Blackout windows: acceptable with one change — the MSA should include a clear definition of "production endpoints tied to this order form" (we can tie to project IDs in the order form). Also propose adding an emergency maintenance clause allowing unscheduled work for security patches with 8-hr notice where feasible.
- Credit caps: we cannot accept an uncapped aggregation of credits. Redwood standard is an invoice-month cap equal to 100% of monthly subscription fees; we'll include explicit examples in the SLA language to avoid confusion. If EdgeCloud insists on different caps, provide specific commercial rationale (e.g., internal procurement requirement) and we can evaluate.
- Response SLA wording: prefer to avoid absolute commitments on troubleshooting time (time to resolution) but will accept initial response times as Vanessa outlined. We will add an "Escalation Ladder" exhibit to the order form listing contact tiers and expected acknowledgement timeframes.

Attached: MSA_v3_redlines.docx (track changes) — redline includes suggested edits to section 5 (Maintenance), section 8 (Credits), and an exhibit for the escalation ladder.

Please review and provide one consolidated set of redlines back to us; duplicative parallel threads slow procurement.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: MSA_v3_redlines.docx

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@edgecloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@edgecloud.com, Legal Team <legal@edgecloud.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — MSA + Order Form (staffing/maintenance)

Kimberly / Vanessa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the concrete alternatives. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing your redlines:

- Blackout definition: we can accept linking the blackout to project IDs. We will run that by procurement but this should be fine.
- Emergency maintenance: the security patch carve-out is acceptable if Redwood commits to a written post-facto report within 48 hours listing impacted customers and mitigation steps.

Remaining sticking point: credit math. Our CFO insisted on a predictable simple schedule (their preference: 10% @ 2 hrs, 30% @ 8 hrs) because their accounting systems can't easily take tiered percentage steps tied to detection algorithms.

Can Redwood accept a negotiated exception limited to EdgeCloud with a commercial addendum on the order form that codifies the 10%/30% bands and a capped monthly credit of 150% of monthly fees (EdgeCloud-specific commercial addendum)? This would be an exception to Redwood's standard cap but limited to our account and under a defined addendum.

If Redwood legal is open to an account-specific addendum, we can move to procurement and e-sign next week. If not, we will need to escalate to finance for a waiver.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Director, Cloud Ops — EdgeCloud
